steps.text: A flaky test is either time, ordering or shared state. The name mentions a business-day window, so time is the first suspect.
Let me reproduce it first — a flake that passes on rerun tells me more than the stack trace does.

steps.result:
00:02 +7 -1: window rolls over at the business-day boundary [E]
  Expected: 3
    Actual: 2
  test/escrow/timeline_window_test.dart 61:7

00:02 +7 -1: Some tests failed.

steps.text: Reproduced. It expects three contingencies in the rolled-over window and gets two.

There it is. The test calls `DateTime.now()` directly, so when the suite happens to run across a real day boundary the business-day delta to the seeded records grows by one — three over a weekend — and the first record falls outside the window. It is not the timeline calculator that is flaky — it is the test's clock.

Green, and now deterministic. `ContingencyWindow` already accepted an injectable `now`; the test simply was not using it.

I did not touch production code — the flake was entirely in the test's use of the wall clock.
